2.title: First Steps, after Millet
2.note: A mother holds up a toddler while the father kneels with open arms in a garden, so 'supporting is its own strength' reads at once and the earth is right there.

critique.feedback: The mother steadying the child from behind while the father waits with open arms is a picture of 'supporting is its own strength'. It reads in a second, the Van Gogh brushwork is recognisable, and the figures sit well inside a vertical crop.

3.title: The Knitting Lesson
3.commons: File:Jean-François Millet - The Knitting Lesson - 106-1939 - Saint Louis Art Museum.jpg
3.note: A mother guides a girl through her first stitches, with the yarn tangled on her lap: a beginner sorting the threads one at a time, which fits 'get organized' and 'boring beats bold'.

critique.feedback: The picture shows the Image line's 'sorts the threads' literally, as a tangle of yarn being worked through with patient help, and it is portrait format, so it fills 1080x1920 without panning. It goes well with 'Boring beats bold'.

4.title: The Fortune Teller
4.note: A naive young man has his palm read while she slips off his ring: someone shopping for a better answer who does not see what is happening, which matches 'ask once'.

critique.risk: none (palm-reading is itself a kind of divination, which suits the subject)
critique.feedback: A young man in a feather hat holds out his palm to be read by a smiling fortune teller, which pairs directly with 'asking again for a better answer'. The two large faces hold up full-frame and panning.

6.title: Fight with Cudgels (Duelo a garrotazos)
6.commons: File:Francisco de Goya y Lucientes - Duelo a garrotazos.jpg
6.note: Two men club each other while both sink knee-deep in the ground, so the viewer sees right away that fighting to the end costs both sides; there is no fire or army, and only a little blood on the faces.

critique.risk: mild: two men swinging clubs, but no blood and the fight is the hexagram's subject, so not capped
critique.feedback: Two men knee-deep in mud, still swinging, show 'pushing to the end costs you' at a glance, and the two figures hold up across a wide pan.

9.title: Dancers Practicing at the Barre
9.commons: File:Degas - Dancers Practicing at the Bar.JPG
9.note: Two dancers drilling at the barre in an empty room, not on stage yet: 'not yet, work on yourself meanwhile'.

critique.feedback: Two dancers drilling at the barre in an empty studio fits 'not yet, work on yourself meanwhile', and Degas dancers are widely known. The crop has to hold on the upper half, because the lower half is bare floor.

10.title: Tiger in a Tropical Storm (Surprised!)
10.note: A startled, snarling tiger in the grass reads at once as a temper you must step carefully around, and Treading's classic image is stepping on the tiger's tail.

critique.feedback: A crouched, snarling tiger in a storm reads as 'someone with a temper' at once, and the whole short is about stepping carefully around it. It is well known, the colours are strong, and the pan can end on the tiger at lower left.

11.title: First Steps (after Millet)
11.note: A father kneels with both arms held out as his child walks toward him, a plain and warm picture of reaching someone that fits 'Peace is contact' and 'Who haven't you reached lately?'.

critique.feedback: A father on his knees reaching out to a child taking its first steps is warm, calm and about contact, which answers 'Who haven't you reached lately?' almost word for word. The pastel palette holds up full-frame. The only weakness is the width: in a 9:16 pan the father and the child fall in separate halves, so the pan has to travel from his open arms to her.

13.title: The Peasant Dance
13.note: In the foreground a man pulls a woman by the hand as they run toward the open line of dancers, while a girl teaches a small child the steps, so the pan shows newcomers being brought into the village dance, which matches 'let new people walk up'.

critique.risk: none (mild: drinking and a kissing couple at the table on the left, a sword at the dancer's hip; none of it reads badly at speed)
critique.feedback: A whole village dancing together reads as fellowship at once, and a pan that ends on the couple hurrying in to join the ring gives a literal image for 'let new people walk up'. Before use, trim the black border and get a higher-resolution file, because the 897 px height will look soft blown up to 1920.

17.title: The End of the Working Day (Fin du travail)
17.commons: File:Brooklyn Museum - Fin du travail (The End of the Working Day) - Jules Breton.jpg
17.note: Field workers carry their tools home as the sun goes down, which matches 'Day's done. Go in, rest.' and the title says it too.

critique.feedback: Workers walking home through the field at sunset read at once as 'day's done, go in'. The glowing sun and the large central figures hold up full-frame, though few viewers will know the painting.

18.title: The Floor Scrapers
18.commons: File:Gustave Caillebotte - The Floor Planers - Google Art Project.jpg
18.note: Workers on their knees scraping off a dark old floor strip by strip to the clean wood underneath shows slow, careful repair of what is under the surface (the men are shirtless, not nude).

critique.feedback: Men on their knees scraping an old floor back to bare wood show repair done slowly and properly, which ties to 'Rushed repairs don't hold'. The strong perspective works well as a pan.

19.title: The Sower (Sower with Setting Sun)
19.commons: File:The Sower - painting by Van Gogh.jpg
19.note: A man sows seed in a hurry under a huge setting sun with ripe wheat behind him, which fits 'go, but plan' and 'every spring has an autumn'. This is a museum photo; the 2500px Commons file is a pen drawing and the 3870px one is scanned from a book, so I rejected both.

critique.feedback: A man sowing under a huge sun is 'go, but plan' and 'every spring has an autumn' in one image, and the strong Van Gogh colour and brushwork hold up full-frame.

20.title: Sazai Hall at the Temple of the Five Hundred Arhats (Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji)
20.note: A row of travellers who climbed to a temple balcony stand in the centre of the print looking out over the country to Fuji, one pointing, porters resting after the climb, so it shows 'go and look' with the figures large and centred for a 9:16 pan.

critique.feedback: People climbed to a high balcony and are looking and pointing at Fuji, which is exactly 'go and look'. The Hokusai style is recognisable, and the flat, clean colours and large foreground figures pan well in a vertical frame, even though Fuji itself is small.

21.title: The Woodcutter
21.commons: File:Fernidand Hodler - The Woodcutter - Google Art Project.jpg
21.note: One man swinging an axe with his whole body at the trunk in his way shows 'bite down' as effort, with no blood; the portrait format needs no pan.

critique.feedback: A man at the top of an axe swing is 'bite down, it won't clear by itself' with no explanation needed. The canvas is already vertical with a bold, clean silhouette, so it is ideal full-frame. The axe is aimed at a tree, so there is no violence risk.

22.title: A Goldsmith in his Shop
22.note: A goldsmith carefully weighs a ring on tiny scales, with polished ornaments on the shelf behind him, while a betrothed couple waits beside him on the biggest decision of their lives. Careful craft on small things sits next to a choice that polish cannot make.

critique.risk: minor: the goldsmith wears a saint's halo (St Eligius), a small religious note most viewers will pass over
critique.feedback: The fit with the copy is good. A goldsmith weighs a ring while a betrothed couple waits, so one sentence can say he handles the polish and they still have to make the decision. The portrait format suits 1080x1920 with little cropping. What it lacks is an instant read. In 4 seconds a scroller sees three people in a shop, and the 'ornament vs. decision' point needs the caption to carry it. The key details are small: the ring on the scale, the jewels on the shelf. The halo also pulls the eye toward a religious reading. A better image would make adornment the whole subject, such as a well-known still life or portrait where people are visibly fussing over finery (a lady at her toilette, someone gilding or polishing a surface) while something bigger is left undone, and without saints. If no stronger image turns up, keep this one: the tie to the copy holds, but it won't land without the sentence.

23.title: The Rescue
23.commons: File:John Everett Millais - The rescue - Google Art Project.jpg
23.note: A fireman carries children down the stairs of a burning house to their mother: things falling apart and someone who stays to help the people who depend on him. It is vertical, so it suits the Reel frame. The children's legs are bare, and the scene is otherwise safe.

critique.risk: mild: children carried out of a house fire, but the rescue has already succeeded and the mood is relief
critique.feedback: A fireman carries children out of a collapsing, burning house to their mother. It fits 'don't run, help those below you' and 'who depends on you?' exactly, and the tall canvas suits 9:16, though few viewers will know it.

26.title: The Star (L'Étoile)
26.note: A dancer steps out alone into the stage light, with the other dancers waiting in the wings, which shows years of practice finally going public; it is a pastel, and the file is portrait.

critique.risk: minor: those who know Degas may link the man in black in the wings to dancers' patrons; most viewers won't notice
critique.feedback: A dancer lit at centre stage after years of unseen practice is 'go public' in one frame, and the portrait format fills a vertical screen.

29.title: Pilgrims at Kirifuri Waterfall on Mount Kurokami (A Tour of Waterfalls in Various Provinces)
29.commons: File:Katsushika Hokusai, Japanese - Pilgrims at Kirifuri Waterfall on Mount Kurokami in Shimotsuke Province - Google Art Project.jpg
29.note: Water pouring down over ledge after ledge, filling each and flowing on, is the Abyss image 'water upon water' and 'fill it, flow on', and it is tall enough to fill the vertical frame.

critique.feedback: Water pouring over rock in many repeated channels matches 'water upon water... fill it, flow on'. The print is vertical, bold and graphic, so it fills a phone screen well, and Hokusai's style is widely recognised.

31.title: Dust Motes Dancing in the Sunbeams
31.note: The critic's suggestion: a bare portrait-format room with a bright diagonal shaft of sunlight falling across the empty floor, which shows 'make room' and 'an emptiness that lets something in', with more contrast than White Doors.

critique.feedback: An empty, sunlit room with light coming in shows 'receives others through emptiness' and 'make room' at a glance, and the near-vertical canvas fills a 9:16 frame cleanly with no bad crop.

32.title: The Sower (Sower with Setting Sun)
32.commons: File:Van Gogh - Sämann bei untergehender Sonne.jpeg
32.note: The critic's suggested fix: a bright yellow sun and violet field with one man striding the same way and scattering seed at every step, so 'show up again, keep moving, same direction' reads at once on a phone.

critique.feedback: A man walking one way across the field, repeating one throw of seed after another, fits 'show up again, keep moving, same direction'. It is bright and clearly Van Gogh, and the pan from the sun to the sower works well.

33.title: The Fighting Temeraire
33.commons: File:The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg
33.note: An old warship is towed calmly into a sunset on its last trip, a well-known picture of leaving with dignity and no anger; it is not the Turner Houses of Parliament fire that is already approved.

critique.feedback: The old warship being towed off calmly into the sunset is 'leave well, no anger, just distance', and the pan from ship to sun has a clear direction.

34.title: The Horse Fair
34.note: Huge rearing horses held on reins by their handlers show great power kept under control, which fits 'check your aim' without the violence of the Lion Hunt; it is wide, so it pans.

critique.feedback: Huge horses held back by handlers show power that has to be reined in, which fits 'check your aim, know what not to do'. The canvas is very wide (about 2:1), so the pan should start on the rearing black horse and the grey pair in the centre. Parked at either edge it loses the point.

35.title: Woman before the Rising Sun
35.commons: File:Caspar David Friedrich - Frau vor untergehender Sonne.jpg
35.note: Light rising over the land behind a single open-armed figure matches the Image, brightness emerging above the earth. Caveat: the museum's title is disputed between rising and setting sun (the Commons filename says setting), so the on-screen title should say 'Rising Sun'.

critique.feedback: The Image line is 'Brightness emerges above the earth', and here a figure stands with open arms as the sun comes up over the land. The central figure survives a vertical crop and the warm gold carries the drop. One note: Friedrich's Wanderer is already approved, so this is his second back-view figure in the series.

36.title: The Newborn Child
36.commons: File:Georges de La Tour - Newlyborn infant - Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rennes.jpg
36.note: In a dark room a woman cups her hand around a candle so it lights only a sleeping baby. This is a hidden light that is being protected, which fits 'keep your light inside' and the question about what light you are protecting. It is a domestic scene with no religious symbols.

critique.risk: slight: it can read as a Nativity scene, though the title is secular
critique.feedback: A woman cups her hand around a hidden candle in a dark room. The image is literally 'keep your light inside' and 'using dimness to remain bright', and its strong light and dark read well on a phone.

38.title: The Card Players
38.commons: File:Les Joueurs de cartes, par Paul Cézanne.jpg
38.note: Two very different men sit facing each other, one dark and one light, and play one game at a shared table, which shows 'share something, stay different' at a glance and has none of the violence of the Caravaggio.

critique.risk: none (a pipe and a bottle, no drinking scene)
critique.feedback: Two different men set across a table from each other but sharing one game is 'share something, stay different', and the big, simple shapes read well full-frame despite the brown palette.

40.title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows
40.note: A rainbow breaks over the cathedral as the storm clouds move off. The painting is close to square (1.25:1), so a centre crop keeps the spire and most of the arc on screen together, and 'the storm has passed' reads at a glance as 'the pressure's finally off'.

critique.risk: none (the cathedral is scenery, not a religious message)
critique.feedback: A storm breaking into a rainbow over wet meadows shows thunder and rain passing and the pressure lifting, and the rainbow can carry 'let the grudges go' in one plain sentence. The spire and the rainbow's right leg fit a 9:16 frame, so a pan from spire to rainbow works.

41.title: The Gleaners
41.commons: File:Jean-François Millet - Gleaners - Google Art Project 2.jpg
41.note: Women picking up the stalks the harvest left behind shows having less than before, and gleaning was a custom where farmers left some grain for others, which fits 'give what you can'. Caveat: poor women placed next to 'having less' could draw the same kind of risk note as the Daumier.

critique.feedback: The painting is very well known. Women pick up the leftover grain while the big harvest sits far off, which shows 'having less' and making do with it without drama. The three bent figures give the pan a clear path.

42.title: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind)
42.commons: File:Winslow Homer - Breezing Up (A Fair Wind) - Google Art Project.jpg
42.note: Boys in a heeling catboat run before a fair wind: good conditions and people using them now. This fits 'go now' and Increase's wind image.

critique.feedback: A boat heeling hard with the wind in its sail is 'Increase says: go now' as a picture, and the clear, bright seascape pans well across its width.

43.title: Cicero Denounces Catiline
43.commons: File:Cicero Denounces Catiline in the Roman Senate by Cesare Maccari.png
43.note: One man stands in front of the Senate and names a wrong to the face of the man sitting alone on the empty benches, with only his raised arm and no force, which is the 'call it out, say it openly' of the copy, and the bright white togas hold up full-frame.

critique.risk: none (ancient political scene, nothing current; the accused is isolated but not caricatured)
critique.feedback: One man standing up in the open Senate and calling another out matches 'call something out' and 'say it openly, no force' exactly, and a left-to-right pan from Cicero to Catiline sitting alone tells the story without words. This copy is 833 px high and looks upscaled and colour-boosted, so fetch a higher-resolution, less saturated reproduction before rendering.

44.title: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
44.commons: File:Le Tricheur à l'as de carreau - Georges de La Tour - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 1972 8.jpg
44.note: A rich young man is charmed at cards while the woman's sideways glance and the ace hidden behind the cheat's back give the trick away: 'charm can be the warning'.

critique.feedback: The glamorous table with the cheat hiding aces behind his back is 'charm can be the warning' exactly, and the sideways glances land fast. Make sure the pan starts on or passes over the hidden aces at the left edge, because that detail carries the point.

46.title: The Large Piece of Turf
46.commons: File:Albrecht Dürer - The Large Piece of Turf, 1503 - Google Art Project.jpg
46.note: A vertical study of grass stems and dandelions growing up out of visible soil and roots, close to 'within the earth, wood grows'; it shows small things rising and fits 'Growing slower than you want? Small steps, piled up'. Dürer is already in the series with Young Hare.

critique.feedback: Grass pushing up out of dark soil is almost literally 'within the earth, wood grows'; it fits 'small steps, piled up'; and it is a well-known vertical study that holds up full-frame.

47.title: Man with a Hoe
47.commons: File:Millet, Jean-François - Man with a Hoe - Google Art Project.jpg
47.note: One worn-out man leaning on his hoe in dry, stony, thistle-choked ground, too tired to speak but still working, matches the lake without water and 'Words fail here. Actions don't.'; he is large and central, so a pan keeps him in frame.

critique.risk: minor: it was read as a protest image about exploited labour in the 1860s, but nothing in it reads as political to a viewer today
critique.feedback: A worn-out labourer leaning on his hoe in dry, stony ground shows 'lake without water' and exhaustion at once, and the large central figure crops cleanly to vertical. It shows endurance more than resolve, so the sentence should say he keeps working.

48.title: Girl at the Well
48.commons: File:Elizabeth Jane Gardner Girl at the well.jpg
48.note: The well rope and pulley fill the top of the frame and the girl pours out a full bucket of water, so 'lengthen the rope, the water is always there' reads at once; it is not famous, the original is only 1004 px wide (2000 px tall, so it passes the long-side rule), and the 1280 px download is the original file.

critique.feedback: The rope, pulley, bucket and falling water say 'well' instantly and back up 'the water is always there', and the tall canvas is almost exactly 9:16, which makes up for it being little known.

49.title: The Fighting Temeraire
49.commons: File:The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg
49.note: A small black steam tug tows a ghostly old warship to be broken up under a bright sunset: the new thing replacing the old before anyone was ready, and the painting is bright enough to read full-frame.

critique.feedback: A famous image of the old order being towed away by the new, with the sun setting in the water (fire within the lake). A left-to-right pan runs from the ghostly warship to the sunset, and one sentence ties it to 'trust comes on the last day'.

50.title: An Old Woman Cooking Eggs
50.commons: File:Diego Velazquez - An Old Woman Cooking Eggs - Google Art Project.jpg
50.note: A cooking pot on the fire with every ingredient and utensil laid out in its place is the caldron and 'get set up before you start' in one image.

critique.feedback: A clay pot over a fire, with the ingredients and tools laid out around it, reads as 'the caldron' and 'get set up before you start' straight away. The lighting has strong contrast and the pan from pot to cook works.

51.title: Surprised! (Tiger in a Tropical Storm)
51.note: A tiger crouches wide-eyed as lightning cracks through a jungle storm. It is literally thunder and fright, which matches 'did something just shake you?'. It is famous and reads within a second.

critique.feedback: A startled tiger in a lightning storm is 'did something just shake you?' at a glance. It is widely known, bright, and the tiger is big enough to hold the frame.

52.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
52.commons: File:Katsushika Hokusai - Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Gaifū kaisei) - Google Art Project.jpg
52.note: One still mountain under a calm sky matches the Image of connected mountains and the copy's 'pause'; it is among the most recognizable Japanese prints and is not the Great Wave already used.

critique.feedback: One still, red mountain under calm sky is Keeping Still without a word of explanation, and the bold flat shapes pan cleanly. It is a second Hokusai after the Great Wave, but it looks different enough.

54.title: Woman at a Window
54.commons: File:Caspar David Friedrich - Frau am Fenster - Google Art Project.jpg
54.note: A vertical painting of a woman shut in a bare brown room, looking out an open window at ship masts and bright trees, which fits 'no way out? see the end, this part won't last' with no wedding and no suffering.

critique.risk: minor: a woman shown confined next to 'No power' could read as a comment on women, but she is dignified and looking out, so it stays well under a real risk
critique.feedback: The portrait format fills 9:16 with no cropping. She is shut indoors but looking out at ships' masts, which suits 'no power, no way out? see the end'. One note: Friedrich and the figure seen from behind already appear in the Wanderer, which is among the approved paintings, so the series will repeat itself.

55.title: Noon – Rest from Work (after Millet)
55.commons: File:Vincent van Gogh - The siesta (after Millet) - Google Art Project.jpg
55.note: Harvesters asleep against a full haystack under a blazing noon sky give abundance, 'don't worry' and the sun at noon at once.

critique.feedback: The painting has blazing noon light and a full harvest, and the pair sleep untroubled, so it matches 'don't worry, be the sun at noon'. It is recognisably Van Gogh and bright enough for the drop. It does not match the 'decide' question, though, so the one plain sentence should link it to the 'don't worry' line.

56.title: Kanbara: Night Snow (Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō)
56.note: The critic's suggested print: travellers in straw hats walk quietly through a strange mountain village at night with every door shut, a calm picture of passing through as a guest; there is no fire on the hill, and this MFA scan shows the album's centre fold and corner mounts, so a pan from the lone walker on the left to the pair on the right works best.

critique.feedback: Travellers with hats and umbrellas passing closed houses at night fit 'somewhere new, out of place', but this copy of the print is worn: there is a fold line down the centre, torn corner mounts and flat grey contrast, so full-frame it will look muddy, and the two groups of figures sit far apart for a vertical crop. Use a cleaner museum impression of the same print (the Met, Honolulu or the Brooklyn Museum have crisp ones), or another clean Hiroshige Tokaido print with a single traveller large in the frame arriving at an inn or crossing unfamiliar ground.

57.title: The Young Schoolmistress
57.commons: File:Jean Siméon Chardin - The Young Schoolmistress - WGA04750.jpg
57.note: A girl points out letters one by one to a small child, which shows 'say it again, quiet and steady gets through'; it is a different Chardin from the approved Saying Grace, and it drops the wind link to follow the copy.

critique.feedback: A patient older girl pointing letter by letter for a small child is 'quiet and steady gets through', and a slow pan from the child's face to the pointer to the teacher works. It is a second Chardin after Saying Grace.

58.title: Hip, Hip, Hurrah! Artists' Party at Skagen
58.commons: File:Hipp hipp hurra! Konstnärsfest på Skagen - Peder Severin Krøyer.jpg
58.note: Friends raising their glasses together round a garden table is shared joy, the exact opposite of joy kept alone.

critique.feedback: Friends raising glasses together in dappled sun is 'share it, joy with friends' at a glance. The near-square canvas crops well around the toast and the laughing faces.

59.title: The Bucintoro Returning to the Molo on Ascension Day
59.commons: File:Canaletto - Bucentaur's return to the pier by the Palazzo Ducale - Google Art Project.jpg
59.note: Gondolas scattered across the windy lagoon all head for the Doge's gilded barge and palace on the day of Venice's yearly Marriage of the Sea offering, so a whole scattered city is drawn back to one shared rite and place on the water. It pans well across a wide canvas.

critique.risk: minor: Ascension Day is a church festival, but the image reads as a civic celebration on the water, not as religious
critique.feedback: Gondolas scattered across the water all turn toward one ceremonial barge in front of the Doge's Palace. That matches 'wind over water' and 'remind them where they come from' at a glance, and 'what do you all share?' ties to it in one plain sentence. Canaletto's Venice is widely recognised, and the crisp detail holds up well in a slow pan across the wide frame. It falls short of higher marks because the wind is shown only by a single flag and the scene reads more as a gathering than a scattering.

60.title: Ulysses and the Sirens
60.commons: File:John William Waterhouse - Ulysses and the Sirens - Google Art Project.jpg
60.note: Ulysses has himself tied to the mast so he cannot say yes to the sirens. It is the classic picture of a self-imposed limit, which answers 'saying yes to everything?'. The sirens have bird bodies and are not nude, and the rowers are bare-chested.

critique.risk: none (sirens as bird-women, rowers shirtless but not sexualised)
critique.feedback: Ulysses tied to the mast so he can't say yes to the sirens is 'set limits' in one image, and he sits at the centre of the wide canvas, so the pan lands on him.

62.title: The Lacemaker
62.note: A woman bends close over tiny bobbins and thread, a famous picture of small work done well, which matches 'no big moves, small done well ends well'; it is a Vermeer not already in the approved list.

critique.feedback: A woman bent over tiny, exact handwork is 'small done well ends well' in one glance, and the close crop fills the frame. The one caution: this would be the third Vermeer in the series, after The Milkmaid and Woman Holding a Balance.

63.title: Belshazzar's Feast
63.note: A king at the height of his feast turns to see the writing on the wall. It is a famous image of a peak moment with trouble plainly coming, and it fits 'Prepare now, while it works' and 'What could go wrong?' directly.

critique.risk: none real; a Bible scene with Hebrew letters, but 'the writing on the wall' is an everyday idiom and the scene is warning, not violence
critique.feedback: A king at the height of his feast turns to see the warning on the wall, which matches 'Just finished something big? Stay alert. What could go wrong?' exactly. The idiom is widely known, and the lit king, his outstretched arm and the glowing letters fit a vertical frame with a short pan.

64.title: The Chess Game
64.note: A game in the middle, a hand hovering over a piece, which matches 'not yet', 'sort things out before you move' and 'what goes where'.

critique.feedback: A chess game in mid-play, with a hand deciding where a piece goes, is 'not yet, sort things out before you move' and 'What goes where?' almost word for word. The faces and colours are vivid and the board sits centrally for a vertical crop.

history.title: First Steps, after Millet
history.commons: File:Vincent van Gogh - First Steps.jpg
history.note: A mother holds up a toddler while the father kneels with open arms in a garden, so 'supporting is its own strength' reads at once and the earth is right there.

critique.feedback: The mother steadying the child from behind while the father waits with open arms is a picture of 'supporting is its own strength'. It reads in a second, the Van Gogh brushwork is recognisable, and the figures sit well inside a vertical crop.

history.title: Dancers Practicing at the Barre
history.commons: File:Degas - Dancers Practicing at the Bar.JPG
history.note: Two dancers drilling at the barre in an empty room, not on stage yet: 'not yet, work on yourself meanwhile'.

critique.feedback: Two dancers drilling at the barre in an empty studio fits 'not yet, work on yourself meanwhile', and Degas dancers are widely known. The crop has to hold on the upper half, because the lower half is bare floor.

history.title: The End of the Working Day (Fin du travail)
history.commons: File:Brooklyn Museum - Fin du travail (The End of the Working Day) - Jules Breton.jpg
history.note: Field workers carry their tools home as the sun goes down, which matches 'Day's done. Go in, rest.' and the title says it too.

critique.feedback: Workers walking home through the field at sunset read at once as 'day's done, go in'. The glowing sun and the large central figures hold up full-frame, though few viewers will know the painting.

history.title: The Woodcutter
history.commons: File:Fernidand Hodler - The Woodcutter - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: One man swinging an axe with his whole body at the trunk in his way shows 'bite down' as effort, with no blood; the portrait format needs no pan.

critique.feedback: A man at the top of an axe swing is 'bite down, it won't clear by itself' with no explanation needed. The canvas is already vertical with a bold, clean silhouette, so it is ideal full-frame. The axe is aimed at a tree, so there is no violence risk.

history.title: Pilgrims at Kirifuri Waterfall on Mount Kurokami (A Tour of Waterfalls in Various Provinces)
history.commons: File:Katsushika Hokusai, Japanese - Pilgrims at Kirifuri Waterfall on Mount Kurokami in Shimotsuke Province - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Water pouring down over ledge after ledge, filling each and flowing on, is the Abyss image 'water upon water' and 'fill it, flow on', and it is tall enough to fill the vertical frame.

critique.feedback: Water pouring over rock in many repeated channels matches 'water upon water... fill it, flow on'. The print is vertical, bold and graphic, so it fills a phone screen well, and Hokusai's style is widely recognised.

history.title: The Horse Fair
history.commons: File:Rosa Bonheur, The Horse Fair, 1852–55.jpg
history.note: Huge rearing horses held on reins by their handlers show great power kept under control, which fits 'check your aim' without the violence of the Lion Hunt; it is wide, so it pans.

critique.feedback: Huge horses held back by handlers show power that has to be reined in, which fits 'check your aim, know what not to do'. The canvas is very wide (about 2:1), so the pan should start on the rearing black horse and the grey pair in the centre. Parked at either edge it loses the point.

history.title: Spring (Le Printemps)
history.commons: File:Jean-François Millet (II) 006.jpg
history.note: A rainbow over blossoming trees as the storm clouds pull away: 'thunder and rain arise' and the pressure lifting, seen in a second.

critique.feedback: The storm clearing into spring blossom fits 'thunder and rain... the pressure's off', but a vertical crop cuts off the rainbow at the top-left edge, and the dark sky and brown foreground look muddy on a phone. Nothing in it points to forgiveness. Look for an image where release from a storm is bright and central, such as a clear rainbow over a landscape after rain (for example Constable's rainbow landscapes, or Inness's 'Peace and Plenty'), or a plain, non-religious scene of reconciliation, like two people shaking hands or embracing.

history.title: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
history.commons: File:Le Tricheur à l'as de carreau - Georges de La Tour - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 1972 8.jpg
history.note: A rich young man is charmed at cards while the woman's sideways glance and the ace hidden behind the cheat's back give the trick away: 'charm can be the warning'.

critique.feedback: The glamorous table with the cheat hiding aces behind his back is 'charm can be the warning' exactly, and the sideways glances land fast. Make sure the pan starts on or passes over the hidden aces at the left edge, because that detail carries the point.

history.title: A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery
history.commons: File:Wright of Derby, The Orrery.jpg
history.note: Lamp-lit faces around a model of the planets' revolutions, a new idea being shown to doubters, matching the Image's 'organizes the calendar and clarifies the seasons' with no political scene.

critique.feedback: The orrery ties to the Image line's calendar and seasons, but the short is about a big change nobody believes in until it is finished. A candlelit lecture does not show that, and the lower third is very dark on a phone. Look for a new thing arriving while people doubt it: Turner's 'Rain, Steam and Speed' (the new train charging through) or 'The Fighting Temeraire' (the old ship towed away by a steam tug). The subject should be readable and bright at full frame.

history.title: The Unequal Marriage
history.commons: File:Vasily Pukirev - Неравный брак - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A downcast young bride married to an old official shows a bride with no power and no way out at a glance, so 'this part won't last' lands.

critique.risk: A young bride forced to marry an old man, in a church. Next to 'this part won't last' it reads as waiting for the husband to die, and it pins the hexagram to forced marriage and a religious rite.
critique.feedback: The powerlessness lands, but paired with 'see the end, this part won't last' the image turns into a dark joke about the old groom, which is a real risk. Look for someone confined or subordinate, with no wedding and no suffering, looking toward a way out or a future: Friedrich's 'Woman at a Window' (a figure indoors looking out at masts and the river) or an apprentice or servant looking out a window. The figure should be vertical and clearly readable.

history.title: Hip, Hip, Hurrah! Artists' Party at Skagen
history.commons: File:Hipp hipp hurra! Konstnärsfest på Skagen - Peder Severin Krøyer.jpg
history.note: Friends raising their glasses together round a garden table is shared joy, the exact opposite of joy kept alone.

critique.feedback: Friends raising glasses together in dappled sun is 'share it, joy with friends' at a glance. The near-square canvas crops well around the toast and the laughing faces.

history.title: The Night Watch
history.commons: File:The Nightwatch by Rembrandt - Rijksmuseum.jpg
history.note: A famous picture of a city guard turning out under arms, which reads as 'stay alert, prepare now' for a city that is doing fine.

critique.feedback: The title and its fame carry 'stay alert', but visually it is a dark crowd of armed men, and the 'just finished something big' half is missing. Since only artist and year appear on screen, some viewers will just see a militia. Look for completion paired with vigilance: a finished harvest with a storm building on the horizon, or a ship safely in port while someone watches the weather. The scene should be bright enough to read full-frame.

history.title: Rainy Season in the Tropics
history.commons: File:Frederic Edwin Church - Rainy Season in the Tropics - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A bright double rainbow arches across the middle of the canvas as the rain clears, so 'thunder and rain... the pressure's off' reads at once, with travellers walking on in the lower right.

critique.feedback: A double rainbow over rain-washed mountains says 'the storm has passed' at a glance, so it fits 'the pressure's finally off'. Three things hold it back. The painting is wide (1.5:1), so a 9:16 pan shows only diagonal slices of the arc at any moment, and the full rainbow never appears on screen at once. The travellers are tiny, so no person carries the relief. And nothing in it points to forgiving or dropping a grudge. Something closer would be a better-known after-the-storm image that works in a narrow frame, such as Constable's 'Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows' (rainbow after storm), cropped on the rainbow and cathedral. Better still would be a picture of release between people after conflict (not the Prodigal Son, which is already used).

history.title: The Fighting Temeraire
history.commons: File:The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg
history.note: A small black steam tug tows a ghostly old warship to be broken up under a bright sunset: the new thing replacing the old before anyone was ready, and the painting is bright enough to read full-frame.

critique.feedback: A famous image of the old order being towed away by the new, with the sun setting in the water (fire within the lake). A left-to-right pan runs from the ghostly warship to the sunset, and one sentence ties it to 'trust comes on the last day'.

history.title: Woman at a Window
history.commons: File:Caspar David Friedrich - Frau am Fenster - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A vertical painting of a woman shut in a bare brown room, looking out an open window at ship masts and bright trees, which fits 'no way out? see the end, this part won't last' with no wedding and no suffering.

critique.risk: minor: a woman shown confined next to 'No power' could read as a comment on women, but she is dignified and looking out, so it stays well under a real risk
critique.feedback: The portrait format fills 9:16 with no cropping. She is shut indoors but looking out at ships' masts, which suits 'no power, no way out? see the end'. One note: Friedrich and the figure seen from behind already appear in the Wanderer, which is among the approved paintings, so the series will repeat itself.

history.title: Approaching Storm at Harvest (Aufziehendes Gewitter bei der Ernte)
history.commons: File:Friedrich Voltz - Aufziehendes Gewitter bei der Ernte (1855).jpg
history.note: The harvest is in, piled high on the carts, while a dark storm with visible rain builds on the right: 'just finished something big, stay alert' in one bright, readable image, though the painting is not famous.

critique.feedback: The copy fits very well: the harvest is in and a storm is building, so 'prepare now, while it works' needs no stretching. But almost nobody knows it. At a glance it reads as a calm pastoral, because the threat lives only in the grey cloud on the right. The vertical centre crop shows wagons and animals in water more than the storm. Look for a better-known image of a peak moment with trouble plainly on the way. One candidate is Thomas Cole's 'The Consummation of Empire' from The Course of Empire, a city at its height. Another is a harvest or feast scene where the dark sky or danger takes up a large part of a narrow frame.

history.title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows
history.commons: File:Constable Salisbury meadows.jpg
history.note: A rainbow breaks over the cathedral as the storm clouds move off. The painting is close to square (1.25:1), so a centre crop keeps the spire and most of the arc on screen together, and 'the storm has passed' reads at a glance as 'the pressure's finally off'.

critique.risk: none (the cathedral is scenery, not a religious message)
critique.feedback: A storm breaking into a rainbow over wet meadows shows thunder and rain passing and the pressure lifting, and the rainbow can carry 'let the grudges go' in one plain sentence. The spire and the rainbow's right leg fit a 9:16 frame, so a pan from spire to rainbow works.

history.title: Belshazzar's Feast
history.commons: File:Rembrandt-Belsazar.jpg
history.note: A king at the height of his feast turns to see the writing on the wall. It is a famous image of a peak moment with trouble plainly coming, and it fits 'Prepare now, while it works' and 'What could go wrong?' directly.

critique.risk: none real; a Bible scene with Hebrew letters, but 'the writing on the wall' is an everyday idiom and the scene is warning, not violence
critique.feedback: A king at the height of his feast turns to see the warning on the wall, which matches 'Just finished something big? Stay alert. What could go wrong?' exactly. The idiom is widely known, and the lit king, his outstretched arm and the glowing letters fit a vertical frame with a short pan.

history.title: The Knitting Lesson
history.commons: File:Jean-François Millet - The Knitting Lesson - 106-1939 - Saint Louis Art Museum.jpg
history.note: A mother guides a girl through her first stitches, with the yarn tangled on her lap: a beginner sorting the threads one at a time, which fits 'get organized' and 'boring beats bold'.

critique.feedback: The picture shows the Image line's 'sorts the threads' literally, as a tangle of yarn being worked through with patient help, and it is portrait format, so it fills 1080x1920 without panning. It goes well with 'Boring beats bold'.

history.title: Tiger in a Tropical Storm (Surprised!)
history.commons: File:Henri Rousseau - Surprise!.jpg
history.note: A startled, snarling tiger in the grass reads at once as a temper you must step carefully around, and Treading's classic image is stepping on the tiger's tail.

critique.feedback: A crouched, snarling tiger in a storm reads as 'someone with a temper' at once, and the whole short is about stepping carefully around it. It is well known, the colours are strong, and the pan can end on the tiger at lower left.

history.title: The Floor Scrapers
history.commons: File:Gustave Caillebotte - The Floor Planers - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Workers on their knees scraping off a dark old floor strip by strip to the clean wood underneath shows slow, careful repair of what is under the surface (the men are shirtless, not nude).

critique.feedback: Men on their knees scraping an old floor back to bare wood show repair done slowly and properly, which ties to 'Rushed repairs don't hold'. The strong perspective works well as a pan.

history.title: The Ambassadors
history.commons: File:Hans Holbein the Younger - The Ambassadors - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Two men posed among fur, silk and polished instruments while a distorted skull lies across the floor unresolved: all the polish in the world, and the big question is still there.

critique.risk: mild: the stretched skull is a death symbol, but it does not read at a glance
critique.feedback: The link depends on the anamorphic skull ('fine surfaces hide the big thing'), and a scroller will not decode that smear in 4 seconds. Without it, the viewer sees two rich men beside a table of instruments. In a vertical crop the skull and table are small. Better: a single clear scene of someone busy polishing or adorning while something bigger waits, such as a woman at her toilette or dressing table, or a craftsman gilding a frame. The ornament should be large and obvious, with a vertical or central composition.

history.title: White Doors (Interior from Strandgade 25)
history.commons: File:Vilhelm Hammershøi - Hvide døre. Interiør fra Strandgade 25 - 1913.png
history.note: Open doors onto empty rooms is 'make room' and 'receiving others through emptiness' taken literally, with nothing else in the picture to distract.

critique.feedback: An empty room with open doors fits 'make room' and 'receives through emptiness', and it is portrait format. But it is grey, grainy and low in contrast, and it will look flat on a music drop. Try a luminous empty interior, for example Hammershøi's 'Dust Motes Dancing in the Sunbeams' (1900), a bare room lit by a shaft of sunlight. It says 'empty space that lets something in' and holds up full-frame.

history.title: Woman before the Rising Sun
history.commons: File:Caspar David Friedrich - Frau vor untergehender Sonne.jpg
history.note: Light rising over the land behind a single open-armed figure matches the Image, brightness emerging above the earth. Caveat: the museum's title is disputed between rising and setting sun (the Commons filename says setting), so the on-screen title should say 'Rising Sun'.

critique.feedback: The Image line is 'Brightness emerges above the earth', and here a figure stands with open arms as the sun comes up over the land. The central figure survives a vertical crop and the warm gold carries the drop. One note: Friedrich's Wanderer is already approved, so this is his second back-view figure in the series.

history.title: The Gleaners
history.commons: File:Jean-François Millet - Gleaners - Google Art Project 2.jpg
history.note: Women picking up the stalks the harvest left behind shows having less than before, and gleaning was a custom where farmers left some grain for others, which fits 'give what you can'. Caveat: poor women placed next to 'having less' could draw the same kind of risk note as the Daumier.

critique.feedback: The painting is very well known. Women pick up the leftover grain while the big harvest sits far off, which shows 'having less' and making do with it without drama. The three bent figures give the pan a clear path.

history.title: Oak Grove
history.commons: File:Шишкин И. И. (1887) Дубовая роща.jpg
history.note: Huge old oaks are a plain picture of wood growing out of the earth slowly, a little each year, which fits 'small steps, piled up' and 'don't worry' about pace.

critique.feedback: Grown oaks show the end result, not the slow push upward, and a wide, busy forest turns into generic greenery when panned. Look for something that shows growth in progress: a young tree or sapling rising from the soil among bigger ones, terraced fields, or a figure climbing a long path or stairs step by step. A vertical composition with an obvious upward line would work best.

history.title: An Old Woman Cooking Eggs
history.commons: File:Diego Velazquez - An Old Woman Cooking Eggs - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A cooking pot on the fire with every ingredient and utensil laid out in its place is the caldron and 'get set up before you start' in one image.

critique.feedback: A clay pot over a fire, with the ingredients and tools laid out around it, reads as 'the caldron' and 'get set up before you start' straight away. The lighting has strong contrast and the pan from pot to cook works.

history.title: Noon – Rest from Work (after Millet)
history.commons: File:Vincent van Gogh - The siesta (after Millet) - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Harvesters asleep against a full haystack under a blazing noon sky give abundance, 'don't worry' and the sun at noon at once.

critique.feedback: The painting has blazing noon light and a full harvest, and the pair sleep untroubled, so it matches 'don't worry, be the sun at noon'. It is recognisably Van Gogh and bright enough for the drop. It does not match the 'decide' question, though, so the one plain sentence should link it to the 'don't worry' line.

history.title: Family Reunion
history.commons: File:Réunion de famille - Frédéric Bazille - musée d'Orsay RF 2749.jpg
history.note: A whole family gathered on the terrace of their home answers 'remind them where they come from' and 'what do you all share'. The file is a photo taken in the museum but cropped to the edges of the canvas, so the whole painting shows.

critique.feedback: The family is gathered but everyone looks off in a different direction. That fits 'drifting apart' once someone explains it, but at a glance it is a posed group portrait of strangers, and it is too wide and full of small figures for the pan. Better: an image where scattered people are clearly drawn back together around something they share, such as a family around one table or hearth, a harvest or village festival, or people gathering at a common landmark. The shared centre should be large and obvious.

history.title: The Chess Game
history.commons: File:The Chess Game (Sofonisba Anguissola) 1555 (4096x3236px).jpg
history.note: A game in the middle, a hand hovering over a piece, which matches 'not yet', 'sort things out before you move' and 'what goes where'.

critique.feedback: A chess game in mid-play, with a hand deciding where a piece goes, is 'not yet, sort things out before you move' and 'What goes where?' almost word for word. The faces and colours are vivid and the board sits centrally for a vertical crop.

history.title: Young Woman Powdering Herself
history.commons: File:Young Woman Powdering Herself Georges Seurat.jpg
history.note: A woman in portrait format, absorbed in dabbing powder on at a tiny ornate dressing table, reads at once as 'busy polishing the surface' and fits 'Polish can't make big decisions'; the painted dot border is Seurat's own and part of the canvas.

critique.risk: Mild: corset and cleavage sit at the centre of a vertical crop, and the painting is often read as gently mocking its sitter (Seurat's mistress), which could make 'polish' look like a jab at a woman rather than at a habit. Not enough to cap the score, but noticeable.
critique.feedback: Powdering matches 'polishing' and adornment (the meaning of 22), and the pointillist dots look good full-frame. The problem is the angle: the image says vanity, not 'fine for small things, wrong for big decisions', and the low-cut bodice pulls the eye in a 9:16 crop. Try an image where careful decoration clearly sits beside something unresolved: an artisan gilding or lacquering a small object, a still life or ornament painted with obvious care, or a figure fussing over a detail while a letter or a decision waits on the table. Avoid pictures where a woman grooming herself is the subject.

history.title: Dust Motes Dancing in the Sunbeams
history.commons: File:Hammershøi Dust motes dancing.jpg
history.note: The critic's suggestion: a bare portrait-format room with a bright diagonal shaft of sunlight falling across the empty floor, which shows 'make room' and 'an emptiness that lets something in', with more contrast than White Doors.

critique.feedback: An empty, sunlit room with light coming in shows 'receives others through emptiness' and 'make room' at a glance, and the near-vertical canvas fills a 9:16 frame cleanly with no bad crop.

history.title: The Large Piece of Turf
history.commons: File:Albrecht Dürer - The Large Piece of Turf, 1503 - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A vertical study of grass stems and dandelions growing up out of visible soil and roots, close to 'within the earth, wood grows'; it shows small things rising and fits 'Growing slower than you want? Small steps, piled up'. Dürer is already in the series with Young Hare.

critique.feedback: Grass pushing up out of dark soil is almost literally 'within the earth, wood grows'; it fits 'small steps, piled up'; and it is a well-known vertical study that holds up full-frame.

history.title: Grandfather Telling a Story (Der Grossvater erzählt eine Geschichte)
history.commons: File:Anker Grossvater erzählt eine Geschichte 1884.jpg
history.note: Children gather around their grandfather on a farmhouse porch as he tells a story, with a young woman walking in to join them; this puts 'Remind them where they come from' in one scene with a large, obvious centre. It is landscape and the file is a mid-quality scan (1579 px), so the pan should rest on the grandfather and children.

critique.feedback: The painting is warm and pans well across the figures, and a grandfather's story does match 'remind them where they come from'. But it shows a group that is already together, so nothing in it reads as dispersion or drifting apart, and none of the Image (wind over water, offerings, a temple) appears. It is also barely known. Find a scene where scattered people are drawn back to a shared centre: a congregation or crowd converging on a temple or shrine, a festival or harvest offering that brings a village together, or boats and figures scattered across wind-ruffled water heading for one landmark. The shared rite or place should be the visual centre, not a single family's porch.

history.title: A Goldsmith in his Shop
history.commons: File:Petrus Christus 003.jpg
history.note: A goldsmith carefully weighs a ring on tiny scales, with polished ornaments on the shelf behind him, while a betrothed couple waits beside him on the biggest decision of their lives. Careful craft on small things sits next to a choice that polish cannot make.

critique.risk: minor: the goldsmith wears a saint's halo (St Eligius), a small religious note most viewers will pass over
critique.feedback: The fit with the copy is good. A goldsmith weighs a ring while a betrothed couple waits, so one sentence can say he handles the polish and they still have to make the decision. The portrait format suits 1080x1920 with little cropping. What it lacks is an instant read. In 4 seconds a scroller sees three people in a shop, and the 'ornament vs. decision' point needs the caption to carry it. The key details are small: the ring on the scale, the jewels on the shelf. The halo also pulls the eye toward a religious reading. A better image would make adornment the whole subject, such as a well-known still life or portrait where people are visibly fussing over finery (a lady at her toilette, someone gilding or polishing a surface) while something bigger is left undone, and without saints. If no stronger image turns up, keep this one: the tie to the copy holds, but it won't land without the sentence.

history.title: The Bucintoro Returning to the Molo on Ascension Day
history.commons: File:Canaletto - Bucentaur's return to the pier by the Palazzo Ducale - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Gondolas scattered across the windy lagoon all head for the Doge's gilded barge and palace on the day of Venice's yearly Marriage of the Sea offering, so a whole scattered city is drawn back to one shared rite and place on the water. It pans well across a wide canvas.

critique.risk: minor: Ascension Day is a church festival, but the image reads as a civic celebration on the water, not as religious
critique.feedback: Gondolas scattered across the water all turn toward one ceremonial barge in front of the Doge's Palace. That matches 'wind over water' and 'remind them where they come from' at a glance, and 'what do you all share?' ties to it in one plain sentence. Canaletto's Venice is widely recognised, and the crisp detail holds up well in a slow pan across the wide frame. It falls short of higher marks because the wind is shown only by a single flag and the scene reads more as a gathering than a scattering.

history.title: The Fortune Teller
history.commons: File:The Fortune Teller-Caravaggio (Louvre).jpg
history.note: A naive young man has his palm read while she slips off his ring: someone shopping for a better answer who does not see what is happening, which matches 'ask once'.

critique.risk: none (palm-reading is itself a kind of divination, which suits the subject)
critique.feedback: A young man in a feather hat holds out his palm to be read by a smiling fortune teller, which pairs directly with 'asking again for a better answer'. The two large faces hold up full-frame and panning.

history.title: The Meeting (Bonjour Monsieur Courbet)
history.commons: File:Gustave Courbet - Bonjour Monsieur Courbet - Musée Fabre.jpg
history.note: On a sunny road a traveller stops to greet his patron and they raise their hats: good times shown as contact on the move, which fits 'contact, not a vacation' and 'who haven't you reached'.

critique.feedback: It fits 'peace is contact' and 'who haven't you reached lately?', with a friendly greeting on a road under a wide sky. The problem is that at a glance it reads as three men standing in a field, few viewers know it, and the handshake gesture is small and off-centre. A painting with a warm, obvious act of reaching someone would land better: an embrace, a reunion, people crowded around one table, or a letter being handed over, from a well-known artist.

history.title: The Sower (Sower with Setting Sun)
history.commons: File:The Sower - painting by Van Gogh.jpg
history.note: A man sows seed in a hurry under a huge setting sun with ripe wheat behind him, which fits 'go, but plan' and 'every spring has an autumn'. This is a museum photo; the 2500px Commons file is a pen drawing and the 3870px one is scanned from a book, so I rejected both.

critique.feedback: A man sowing under a huge sun is 'go, but plan' and 'every spring has an autumn' in one image, and the strong Van Gogh colour and brushwork hold up full-frame.

history.title: The Rescue
history.commons: File:John Everett Millais - The rescue - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A fireman carries children down the stairs of a burning house to their mother: things falling apart and someone who stays to help the people who depend on him. It is vertical, so it suits the Reel frame. The children's legs are bare, and the scene is otherwise safe.

critique.risk: mild: children carried out of a house fire, but the rescue has already succeeded and the mood is relief
critique.feedback: A fireman carries children out of a collapsing, burning house to their mother. It fits 'don't run, help those below you' and 'who depends on you?' exactly, and the tall canvas suits 9:16, though few viewers will know it.

history.title: Ploughing in the Nivernais
history.commons: File:Rosa Bonheur - Ploughing in Nevers - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Two ox teams plough one long furrow in a line: slow, steady work in one direction, which fits 'keep moving, same direction'. It is wide, so a left-to-right pan follows the furrow.

critique.feedback: The slow line of oxen ploughing in one direction fits 'keep moving, same direction', but at a glance it reads as a farm scene and doesn't clearly say 'show up again'. It is also a 2:1 canvas, so the figures are small while it pans. A better choice would show one repeated task done day after day, or steady forward motion, with a large central subject that fills a vertical frame. Examples: Millet's The Gleaners or The Angelus, a lone figure walking a long road, or a weaver or spinner at work.

history.title: The Newborn Child
history.commons: File:Georges de La Tour - Newlyborn infant - Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rennes.jpg
history.note: In a dark room a woman cups her hand around a candle so it lights only a sleeping baby. This is a hidden light that is being protected, which fits 'keep your light inside' and the question about what light you are protecting. It is a domestic scene with no religious symbols.

critique.risk: slight: it can read as a Nativity scene, though the title is secular
critique.feedback: A woman cups her hand around a hidden candle in a dark room. The image is literally 'keep your light inside' and 'using dimness to remain bright', and its strong light and dark read well on a phone.

history.title: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind)
history.commons: File:Winslow Homer - Breezing Up (A Fair Wind) - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Boys in a heeling catboat run before a fair wind: good conditions and people using them now. This fits 'go now' and Increase's wind image.

critique.feedback: A boat heeling hard with the wind in its sail is 'Increase says: go now' as a picture, and the clear, bright seascape pans well across its width.

history.title: Prisoners Exercising (The Prison Courtyard)
history.commons: File:Vincent van Gogh - The Prison Courtyard (1890).jpg
history.note: Prisoners walk in a circle between high walls, and one bare-headed man looks out at the viewer. The confinement reads as oppression at once, and the one man looking out suggests someone who keeps his purpose. It is vertical. It fits 'speaking up and nobody listens' less directly. The first choice, Repin's Barge Haulers, was ruled out because Repin died in 1930.

critique.risk: mild: a prison scene, grim but not violent
critique.feedback: The walled-in circle of prisoners says 'oppression' instantly and the tall format suits the frame. But it shows futility and loss of will, while the copy says 'hold your purpose' and 'actions, not words'. It needs a figure who is constrained or ignored yet keeps working at something, so one plain sentence could say 'keep going anyway'. Examples: a lone figure pressing on against wind or a crowd, or someone carrying a heavy load uphill.

history.title: Surprised! (Tiger in a Tropical Storm)
history.commons: File:Henri Rousseau - Surprise!.jpg
history.note: A tiger crouches wide-eyed as lightning cracks through a jungle storm. It is literally thunder and fright, which matches 'did something just shake you?'. It is famous and reads within a second.

critique.feedback: A startled tiger in a lightning storm is 'did something just shake you?' at a glance. It is widely known, bright, and the tiger is big enough to hold the frame.

history.title: Travelers Among Mountains and Streams
history.commons: File:Fan Kuan - Travelers Among Mountains and Streams - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: In this Song masterpiece, a tiny mule train passes beneath a huge mountain: travellers who are passing through, not staying, which fits 'you're a guest'. It is vertical and suits the Reel. The travellers are very small at the lower right, so a pan should end on them or they will be missed. Fan Kuan's death year is approximate.

critique.feedback: The travelers are specks at the bottom right and invisible on a phone. What shows is a dark brown cliff, and the 1:2 scroll makes a muddy vertical pan with no clear subject. The wanderer and the idea of being a guest need to be visible in the first second: a clearly visible traveler arriving somewhere unfamiliar, at an inn, or at a stranger's door. Examples: a Hiroshige Tōkaidō print with travelers at a post town or inn, a Japanese or Chinese painting where the traveler is a large figure, or a Western genre scene of a stranger being received.

history.title: Ulysses and the Sirens
history.commons: File:John William Waterhouse - Ulysses and the Sirens - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: Ulysses has himself tied to the mast so he cannot say yes to the sirens. It is the classic picture of a self-imposed limit, which answers 'saying yes to everything?'. The sirens have bird bodies and are not nude, and the rowers are bare-chested.

critique.risk: none (sirens as bird-women, rowers shirtless but not sexualised)
critique.feedback: Ulysses tied to the mast so he can't say yes to the sirens is 'set limits' in one image, and he sits at the centre of the wide canvas, so the pan lands on him.

history.title: First Steps (after Millet)
history.commons: File:Vincent van Gogh - First Steps.jpg
history.note: A father kneels with both arms held out as his child walks toward him, a plain and warm picture of reaching someone that fits 'Peace is contact' and 'Who haven't you reached lately?'.

critique.feedback: A father on his knees reaching out to a child taking its first steps is warm, calm and about contact, which answers 'Who haven't you reached lately?' almost word for word. The pastel palette holds up full-frame. The only weakness is the width: in a 9:16 pan the father and the child fall in separate halves, so the pan has to travel from his open arms to her.

history.title: The Sower
history.commons: File:Jean-François Millet - The Sower - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: One large figure in a tall frame strides forward, repeating the same throw row after row, which fits 'show up again' and 'keep moving, same direction'.

critique.feedback: A man striding one way and throwing seed on every step fits 'show up again, same direction', and the portrait format fills the frame without a pan. The problem is how dark it is: brown on brown with a dim sky, so on a phone it will look muddy, the thrown seed is almost invisible and the idea of repetition is lost. A lighter version would land better, such as Van Gogh's 'The Sower' (1888) with its big yellow sun, which carries the same stride and gesture and is better known. Another option is a bright scene of repeated labour, like rows already sown or a figure walking a long straight furrow.

history.title: The Fog Warning
history.commons: File:Winslow Homer - The Fog Warning - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: A lone fisherman with a heavy catch keeps rowing through rough water as fog closes in, with nobody to call to, so it reads as 'hold your purpose' and 'actions, not words' rather than defeat.

critique.feedback: A lone man rowing hard toward a distant ship as fog closes in does suggest 'stake your life on your purpose' and 'actions, not words', since nobody could hear him call from there. At first glance, though, it reads as sea adventure or danger, not the hexagram's feeling of being hemmed in, drained and unheard (a lake with no water). The ship that gives it its meaning is tiny at the far right and may be missed in a quick pan. Something that shows a person cut off or confined but still working would land faster: a figure labouring alone in a dry, cracked or barren place, or someone set apart from a crowd that is not listening. If this painting stays, the pan should end on the ship.

history.title: Goyu: Women Stopping Travelers (Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō)
history.commons: File:Goyu LCCN2008660626.jpg
history.note: Innkeepers grab travelers in the middle of a post-town street to pull them into their inn, so the viewer sees at once that these are strangers arriving somewhere as guests, which fits 'You're a guest. Act like one.'

critique.risk: Two inn touts are grabbing a traveller by the neck and dragging him, played for slapstick, so the traveller comes across as a victim of rough handling. That works against the calm 'you're a guest, act like one' message.
critique.feedback: The idea of a traveller in a strange town is there, but the main action is a comic tussle, the opposite of 'keep it brief, be a careful guest'. The figures are small inside a bordered print with a text panel, and cropped to 9:16 the scene turns into a jumble. A better choice is a lone traveller calmly moving through an unfamiliar place, such as a Hiroshige Tōkaidō print of a single walker on a mountain pass or arriving at dusk (for example 'Hakone' or 'Kanbara: Night Snow'), or a Western image of a solitary wayfarer with a pack. The frame should show one figure clearly, small against a big and unfamiliar landscape, ideally with a fire or light on a hill to echo 'fire on the mountain'.

history.title: The Sower (Sower with Setting Sun)
history.commons: File:Van Gogh - Sämann bei untergehender Sonne.jpeg
history.note: The critic's suggested fix: a bright yellow sun and violet field with one man striding the same way and scattering seed at every step, so 'show up again, keep moving, same direction' reads at once on a phone.

critique.feedback: A man walking one way across the field, repeating one throw of seed after another, fits 'show up again, keep moving, same direction'. It is bright and clearly Van Gogh, and the pan from the sun to the sower works well.

history.title: Man with a Hoe
history.commons: File:Millet, Jean-François - Man with a Hoe - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: One worn-out man leaning on his hoe in dry, stony, thistle-choked ground, too tired to speak but still working, matches the lake without water and 'Words fail here. Actions don't.'; he is large and central, so a pan keeps him in frame.

critique.risk: minor: it was read as a protest image about exploited labour in the 1860s, but nothing in it reads as political to a viewer today
critique.feedback: A worn-out labourer leaning on his hoe in dry, stony ground shows 'lake without water' and exhaustion at once, and the large central figure crops cleanly to vertical. It shows endurance more than resolve, so the sentence should say he keeps working.

history.title: Kanbara: Night Snow (Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō)
history.commons: File:Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-16-Kanbara-MFA-01.jpg
history.note: The critic's suggested print: travellers in straw hats walk quietly through a strange mountain village at night with every door shut, a calm picture of passing through as a guest; there is no fire on the hill, and this MFA scan shows the album's centre fold and corner mounts, so a pan from the lone walker on the left to the pair on the right works best.

critique.feedback: Travellers with hats and umbrellas passing closed houses at night fit 'somewhere new, out of place', but this copy of the print is worn: there is a fold line down the centre, torn corner mounts and flat grey contrast, so full-frame it will look muddy, and the two groups of figures sit far apart for a vertical crop. Use a cleaner museum impression of the same print (the Met, Honolulu or the Brooklyn Museum have crisp ones), or another clean Hiroshige Tokaido print with a single traveller large in the frame arriving at an inn or crossing unfamiliar ground.

history.title: Fight with Cudgels (Duelo a garrotazos)
history.commons: File:Francisco de Goya y Lucientes - Duelo a garrotazos.jpg
history.note: Two men club each other while both sink knee-deep in the ground, so the viewer sees right away that fighting to the end costs both sides; there is no fire or army, and only a little blood on the faces.

critique.risk: mild: two men swinging clubs, but no blood and the fight is the hexagram's subject, so not capped
critique.feedback: Two men knee-deep in mud, still swinging, show 'pushing to the end costs you' at a glance, and the two figures hold up across a wide pan.

history.title: Snap the Whip
history.commons: File:Winslow Homer - Snap the Whip (1872).jpg
history.note: Boys run hand in hand in an open chain with free ends that anyone could join, which fits 'keep it open, let new people walk up'; it is wide, so it suits a pan.

critique.feedback: It reads as togetherness, but in snap-the-whip the chain flings its end player off, and the boy on the left has already fallen, which says the opposite of 'let new people walk up'. The line is also closed at both ends. Look for a group with an open circle or a gap, where someone new is visibly being waved or pulled in: an outdoor round dance with an empty hand held out, or a table making room for an arrival. Keep it bright and wide enough to pan.

history.title: Chalk Cliffs on Rügen
history.commons: File:Caspar David Friedrich's Chalk Cliffs on Rügen.jpg
history.note: Three people have walked out to the cliff edge, and one crawls forward to look over it, so the picture shows 'go and look' instead of deciding from a desk; it is a famous Friedrich and is not the Wanderer already in the series.

critique.feedback: People who walked out to the cliff edge, one crawling forward to peer over, fit 'go and look'. But the figures are small and sit at the far left and right corners, so a 9:16 crop of this near-square image cuts the woman in red and the standing man, and what remains is cliffs and sea with no one looking. Find a vertical or centred image where one clearly visible figure has travelled somewhere and is looking out at people or country, or plan a crop that keeps the crawling man and one standing figure.

history.title: The Star (L'Étoile)
history.commons: File:Edgar Degas - Ballet (L'Étoile).jpg
history.note: A dancer steps out alone into the stage light, with the other dancers waiting in the wings, which shows years of practice finally going public; it is a pastel, and the file is portrait.

critique.risk: minor: those who know Degas may link the man in black in the wings to dancers' patrons; most viewers won't notice
critique.feedback: A dancer lit at centre stage after years of unseen practice is 'go public' in one frame, and the portrait format fills a vertical screen.

history.title: The Fighting Temeraire
history.commons: File:The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg
history.note: An old warship is towed calmly into a sunset on its last trip, a well-known picture of leaving with dignity and no anger; it is not the Turner Houses of Parliament fire that is already approved.

critique.feedback: The old warship being towed off calmly into the sunset is 'leave well, no anger, just distance', and the pan from ship to sun has a clear direction.

history.title: The Card Players
history.commons: File:Les Joueurs de cartes, par Paul Cézanne.jpg
history.note: Two very different men sit facing each other, one dark and one light, and play one game at a shared table, which shows 'share something, stay different' at a glance and has none of the violence of the Caravaggio.

critique.risk: none (a pipe and a bottle, no drinking scene)
critique.feedback: Two different men set across a table from each other but sharing one game is 'share something, stay different', and the big, simple shapes read well full-frame despite the brown palette.

history.title: Stump Speaking
history.commons: File:George Caleb Bingham - Stump Speaking.jpg
history.note: A man speaks to a whole crowd in the open with his hands out and no weapons, which fits 'say it openly, no force'; it is a genre scene from an 1850s county election and backs no present-day side, though it is less famous than the others.

critique.risk: political: an election stump speech, painted partly as satire of a smooth-talking candidate, next to 'call something out'
critique.feedback: The speaker is small in a crowd of dozens of faces, so on a phone it reads as a busy crowd scene, and the subject is a campaigning politician, which brings in politics and suggests persuasion more than plain honesty. Look for one large, clearly visible, non-political figure speaking openly and calmly to others: a person standing to address a room or a family, a teacher or elder speaking with an open hand, lit and centred, with no raised fist or weapon.

history.title: Girl at the Well
history.commons: File:Elizabeth Jane Gardner Girl at the well.jpg
history.note: The well rope and pulley fill the top of the frame and the girl pours out a full bucket of water, so 'lengthen the rope, the water is always there' reads at once; it is not famous, the original is only 1004 px wide (2000 px tall, so it passes the long-side rule), and the 1280 px download is the original file.

critique.feedback: The rope, pulley, bucket and falling water say 'well' instantly and back up 'the water is always there', and the tall canvas is almost exactly 9:16, which makes up for it being little known.

history.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
history.commons: File:Katsushika Hokusai - Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Gaifū kaisei) - Google Art Project.jpg
history.note: One still mountain under a calm sky matches the Image of connected mountains and the copy's 'pause'; it is among the most recognizable Japanese prints and is not the Great Wave already used.

critique.feedback: One still, red mountain under calm sky is Keeping Still without a word of explanation, and the bold flat shapes pan cleanly. It is a second Hokusai after the Great Wave, but it looks different enough.

history.title: The Young Schoolmistress
history.commons: File:Jean Siméon Chardin - The Young Schoolmistress - WGA04750.jpg
history.note: A girl points out letters one by one to a small child, which shows 'say it again, quiet and steady gets through'; it is a different Chardin from the approved Saying Grace, and it drops the wind link to follow the copy.

critique.feedback: A patient older girl pointing letter by letter for a small child is 'quiet and steady gets through', and a slow pan from the child's face to the pointer to the teacher works. It is a second Chardin after Saying Grace.

history.title: The Lacemaker
history.commons: File:Johannes Vermeer - The lacemaker (c.1669-1671).jpg
history.note: A woman bends close over tiny bobbins and thread, a famous picture of small work done well, which matches 'no big moves, small done well ends well'; it is a Vermeer not already in the approved list.

critique.feedback: A woman bent over tiny, exact handwork is 'small done well ends well' in one glance, and the close crop fills the frame. The one caution: this would be the third Vermeer in the series, after The Milkmaid and Woman Holding a Balance.

history.title: Children's Round Dance (Kinderreigen)
history.commons: File:Hans Thoma - Kinderreigen (1872).jpg
history.note: A bright outdoor ring of children dancing hand in hand on a meadow, the ring open towards the viewer and the centre girl looking back over her shoulder as if waving you in, so it reads as 'keep it open, let new people walk up' at a glance, and it is wide enough to pan.

critique.feedback: The hand-holding ring reads as fellowship at once, and the figures are large enough to hold up full-frame and panning. The copy is about opening the group ('keep it open, let new people walk up'), though, and this ring is closed, with everyone facing inward. The pan will show a tight circle, not an invitation. Few viewers will know Thoma. A better image would show the same kind of group with a visible gap or an outsider being waved in: a dance or gathering where a hand reaches toward a newcomer, or a figure stepping into an open circle. A well-known painting of that (a Bruegel or Renoir crowd scene with someone arriving) would do better.

history.title: Sazai Hall at the Temple of the Five Hundred Arhats (Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji)
history.commons: File:Sazai hall - 500 Rakan temples.jpg
history.note: A row of travellers who climbed to a temple balcony stand in the centre of the print looking out over the country to Fuji, one pointing, porters resting after the climb, so it shows 'go and look' with the figures large and centred for a 9:16 pan.

critique.feedback: People climbed to a high balcony and are looking and pointing at Fuji, which is exactly 'go and look'. The Hokusai style is recognisable, and the flat, clean colours and large foreground figures pan well in a vertical frame, even though Fuji itself is small.

history.title: A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery
history.commons: File:Wright of Derby, The Orrery.jpg
history.note: A well-known painting of one large, lit, centred elder speaking calmly to a room of adults and children gathered round him, with no crowd, politics or weapon, which fits 'say it openly, speak up, but no force'; it shows him teaching rather than calling someone out.

critique.feedback: This reads as a science lesson or wonder at learning, not as speaking up or calling something out. Nobody in it is voicing anything difficult, and the lecturer is quiet in the background. The picture is mostly near-black, so a vertical crop will look muddy apart from the lit centre. The link needs explaining, which the format does not allow. A better image would show one person standing up to speak plainly in front of others, firm but not violent: a lone figure addressing an assembly or meeting, a hand raised to speak, a truth told to someone's face. Avoid protest or political scenes. Another option follows the Image line ('lake rises above heaven'): water bursting through a barrier or a dam breaking, bright enough to hold full-frame.

history.title: The Peasant Dance
history.commons: File:The Peasant Dance (Bruegel).jpg
history.note: In the foreground a man pulls a woman by the hand as they run toward the open line of dancers, while a girl teaches a small child the steps, so the pan shows newcomers being brought into the village dance, which matches 'let new people walk up'.

critique.risk: none (mild: drinking and a kissing couple at the table on the left, a sword at the dancer's hip; none of it reads badly at speed)
critique.feedback: A whole village dancing together reads as fellowship at once, and a pan that ends on the couple hurrying in to join the ring gives a literal image for 'let new people walk up'. Before use, trim the black border and get a higher-resolution file, because the 897 px height will look soft blown up to 1920.

history.title: Cicero Denounces Catiline
history.commons: File:Cicero Denounces Catiline in the Roman Senate by Cesare Maccari.png
history.note: One man stands in front of the Senate and names a wrong to the face of the man sitting alone on the empty benches, with only his raised arm and no force, which is the 'call it out, say it openly' of the copy, and the bright white togas hold up full-frame.

critique.risk: none (ancient political scene, nothing current; the accused is isolated but not caricatured)
critique.feedback: One man standing up in the open Senate and calling another out matches 'call something out' and 'say it openly, no force' exactly, and a left-to-right pan from Cicero to Catiline sitting alone tells the story without words. This copy is 833 px high and looks upscaled and colour-boosted, so fetch a higher-resolution, less saturated reproduction before rendering.
